clue.text: Agree to put a hundred on a dog

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone backs a greyhound with a hundred-pound bet and says they agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put' only links the definition to the wordplay: C, then ON, then CUR, in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion as someone else.

clue.text: Entertainment can be provided by a page in no time

indicators.note: the page letter goes inside the pair of words for no and time

parts.note: O looks like a zero, nothing
an era is a period of time
P is the standard abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Something fun can be laid on at once by a young attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged musical drama, a form of theatrical show.

clue.text: The fellow a person has little hesitation in making a supervisor

indicators.note: the hesitation sound sits inside the run made by the fellow and a person

parts.note: a chap is a fellow, a man
one can mean a person, as in 'one should'
ER is the short sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: A man hardly pauses before becoming someone's boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone is someone who accompanies and oversees others, often young people.

clue.text: Ballyhoo resulting from criminal enterprise

explanation.surface: Hype that comes out of organised crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is both a din or fuss and a dishonest scheme for making money, such as extortion.

clue.text: Prying characteristic of Cyrano de Bergerac?

definitions.text: Prying characteristic of Cyrano de Bergerac?

parts.words: Prying characteristic of Cyrano de Bergerac?
parts.note: an inquisitive habit, but also, read literally, the quality of having a large nose, Cyrano's famous feature

explanation.surface: Was the famous long-nosed French swordsman also a busybody?
explanation.walkthrough: Cyrano de Bergerac is the hero of Rostand's play, famous for his enormous nose; the answer read as nose-iness fits him literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nosy means poking into other people's business, so the quality is inquisitiveness.

clue.text: As the singer ends broadcast there's a viewer's complaint

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering widely, so these fifteen letters are spread and reassembled

explanation.surface: When a singer finishes on air, someone watching has a grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges AS THE SINGER ENDS. 'complaint' is a medical condition, not a grumble about the programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-sightedness is a defect of eyesight, an ailment affecting how someone sees.

clue.text: Music composed without publicity

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so composed is wrapped around publicity

parts.note: serene means calm, composed
an ad is an advertisement, publicity

explanation.surface: A piece of music was written with no promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' tempts as writing music, but here it means calm; 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a piece sung or played, traditionally beneath a lover's window.

clue.text: Set one's heart on a jug of more modern style

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another is placed above it
the heart of the word one's is its central letter

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug for water

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a jug in an up-to-date design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set one's heart on' looks like a phrase for longing; instead the heart of ONE'S, N, is set on EWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something newer is more recent, of a later fashion.

clue.text: Endorsement certain to capture giant order

indicators.note: the word for certain takes the jumbled letters prisoner, holding them inside

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: order as in putting into order, so the letters of giant are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guaranteed approval will seize a huge order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges the giant's letters into IGNAT, which 'to capture' holds; 'giant order' poses as a huge purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing your name on a document is how you approve or back it.

clue.text: Litter disposal in cars — he'd a solution

indicators.note: a solution is something dissolved and remixed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting rid of rubbish in cars: someone had an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' is not rubbish but an old carried seat; 'disposal' adds to that false picture. 'solution' rearranges IN CARS HE'D A.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter is a covered seat carried on poles by bearers, just like the enclosed chair once used in city streets.

clue.text: Prosecute for money

explanation.surface: Taking someone to court to get paid.
explanation.definitionFit: To wage war is to carry it on, prosecute it; a wage is payment for work.

clue.text: Don't gesticulate so much when calm

explanation.surface: Advice to keep your hands still when you are relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part, read as an instruction, is to wave less; the second describes still water with no swell.
explanation.definitionFit: A calm sea is flat, without any swell or ripples.

clue.text: Quite ordinary woman left behind

indicators.note: the letter for left comes after the woman's name

parts.note: Norma is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An unremarkable woman was abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left behind' reads as abandoned, but 'left' is just L and 'behind' places it after NORMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means usual, typical, unremarkable.

clue.text: Very repetitive but tolerable

indicators.note: repetitive tells us the word for very is said twice over

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: Something extremely dull but bearable.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling or passable; neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Relation taking part in outdoor exercise

indicators.note: the word for relation joins in, sitting inside the word for outdoor

parts.note: in the open means outdoors
a ratio is a relation between two quantities

explanation.surface: A family member joins an open-air workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a relative but is RATIO, a mathematical relation; the 'exercise' is military.
explanation.definitionFit: A military exercise or manoeuvre is an organised action by troops.

clue.text: Worthless silver turned out by an individual on the move

indicators.note: turned means the words for worthless and silver are read backwards together

parts.note: bad means worthless, as in a bad cheque
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fake silver produced by someone who travels around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses BADAG to GADAB, followed by OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is a person who restlessly goes from one place or social event to another.

clue.text: Dressing a group of players getting on together

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
getting on means growing old, aging

explanation.surface: Musicians put on costume while getting along together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on together' suggests harmony, but 'getting on' means growing older.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing a wound is wrapping or covering it with protective strips.

clue.text: A reptile keeping quiet concealed in the ground

indicators.note: the letter for quiet is tucked away inside the word for the ground

parts.note: terrain is a stretch of ground
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A creature lies silently hidden in the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, which is a cold-blooded scaled animal.

clue.text: Devoted as always in the break

indicators.note: the word for always goes inside the word for the break

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
ever means always, as in 'ever faithful'

explanation.surface: Someone remains loyal as usual during the interval.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means showing deep respect, as a devout worshipper does.

clue.text: Born and died in penury

parts.note: née, French for born, introduces a woman's maiden name
d is the abbreviation for died in dates

explanation.surface: Someone was born and died in poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: Need is a state of poverty, lacking money for necessities.

clue.text: Lay into the drink after wife has left

indicators.note: the wife has gone away, so her letter is removed from the drink

parts.note: wassail is a spiced ale drunk at Christmas

explanation.surface: A man hits the bottle after his wife walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay into' looks like attacking a drink but is the definition; 'has left' removes W from WASSAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail someone is to attack them violently, physically or in words.

clue.text: Tray prepared by one making economies — without cash

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the economiser surrounds the cash letter

parts.note: a saver is someone who economises
L, for pound (libra), stands for money

explanation.surface: A serving tray made by a thrifty person with no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside: L goes inside SAVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A salver is a flat ornamental platter for carrying drinks or letters.

clue.text: Poison for which some doctors give no medication

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, the letters lying inside them

explanation.surface: A toxin for which certain doctors offer no remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies within 'give no medication'; 'some doctors' reads as some of the medical profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is the toxic fluid injected by snakes and other creatures.

clue.text: Diets can effect a difference to some extent

indicators.note: to effect is to bring about a change, so these letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Dieting can make a modest improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effect' rearranges DIETS CAN; the definition describes a gap of space between two points.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance is the amount of space separating two points, a gap measured by its extent.

clue.text: Rapid building in the church

indicators.note: the building goes inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hut is a simple building

explanation.surface: Quick construction going on inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rapid' looks like an adjective but is a noun: a stretch of fast water.
explanation.definitionFit: A chute is a steep, fast-flowing stretch of a river, like a waterfall run.

clue.text: Bearing with average sound

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is the one heard when another is spoken

parts.note: the mean is the average of a set of figures

explanation.surface: Carrying something with a fairly normal noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noise but signals a word heard aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's mien is their manner or demeanour, how they carry themselves.

clue.text: Doubtful about transport, and righteous about it

indicators.note: the word for righteous goes round everything before it

parts.note: pious means devout, righteous
re means about, concerning
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A sceptic is unsure about the travel plans but self-righteous about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'about' gives letters while 'about it' is the container signal, wrapping everything before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Precarious means uncertain, insecure, liable to collapse.

clue.text: Bloomers one means to correct

indicators.note: correcting fixes something wrong, so these letters are put right in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone intends to put right their mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like blunders or underwear, but means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Anemones are flowering plants, so they bloom.

clue.text: The youth carrying food back dawdled

indicators.note: the youth holds the other letters inside him

parts.note: a lad is a youth

indicators.note: back means the word for food is read in the other direction

parts.note: an egg is a food

explanation.surface: A young man with food on his back walked slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the food into GGE, which 'carrying' holds; 'food back' poses as a load on the youth's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagged means fell behind, trailed or lingered.
